subject.title: fix(slack): restore HTTP event processing after webhook acknowledgement

question: Should `runDetachedWebhookWork` become a supported public Plugin SDK lifecycle primitive, or should Slack receive a narrower bundled-runtime injection seam?
rationale: The runtime behavior appears correct, but exposing gateway admission semantics through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` creates a durable external contract that cannot be approved from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the generic SDK seam
options.body: Keep the helper in webhook-request-guards, document its synchronous-call and drain-lifetime contract, and require live Slack HTTP proof before merge.

options.title: Use a bundled runtime injection
options.body: Avoid expanding the public Plugin SDK by injecting the independent-root runner through an internal bundled-plugin runtime boundary.

options.title: Pause for sibling webhook audit
options.body: Delay the API decision until maintainers determine whether other ack-first webhook plugins need the same lifecycle primitive.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic SDK seam
recommendation.body: Keep the helper in webhook-request-guards, document its synchronous-call and drain-lifetime contract, and require live Slack HTTP proof before merge.
